title: Domain I: Regulatory & Compliance - CPPB Domain I: Regulatory & Compliance - UCC: Shipping Terms
subject: CPPB Domain I: Regulatory & Compliance

questions.q: If a contract specifies shipping terms as 'FOB Destination,' who holds the risk of loss while the goods are in transit?
questions.explain: Under 'FOB Destination' terms, the seller retains the risk of loss and title to the goods until they are delivered to the specified destination and received by the buyer.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain I: Regulatory & Compliance

questions.q: A shipment of office furniture sent 'FOB Origin' is destroyed in a warehouse fire at the shipping terminal halfway to the agency. Who is legally responsible for the lost goods, and who must file the claim with the carrier?
options: The Seller is responsible and must file the claim.
The Buyer is responsible and must file the claim.
The Carrier is automatically responsible without a claim being filed.
The Seller and Buyer share the liability and must file a joint claim.
questions.explain: Under 'FOB Origin,' title and risk of loss pass to the buyer the moment the goods are handed over to the carrier. The buyer owns the goods during transit and must file any claims for loss or damage.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain I: Regulatory & Compliance

questions.q: If a contract is marked 'FOB Destination, Freight Prepaid', which of the following is true?
options: Buyer pays freight charges; Seller assumes risk of loss.
Seller pays freight charges; Buyer assumes risk of loss during transit.
Buyer pays freight charges; Buyer assumes risk of loss during transit.
Seller pays freight charges; Seller assumes risk of loss during transit.
questions.explain: 'FOB Destination' means the seller retains risk of loss until the goods arrive at the destination. 'Freight Prepaid' means the seller pays the cost of transportation upfront.
